tests.comment: cell_count is asserted at 0 here and at 9 in TM-07, so the two together bracket the writes: a fill that reported success but placed nothing passes one and fails the other.

This used to be allowError, which hid something worse than an error: with no TileSet on the layer the tool answers has_tileset: false as an ordinary success, so the test passed while reporting the fixture was empty — and every write test below was passing on 'the tool correctly refused'. The setup now builds a real single-tile atlas.

A non-zero cell on purpose. The coordinate parser used to drop the string form and fall back to (0, 0), so a test that writes at (0, 0) passes whether the coordinate was understood or discarded — which is exactly why the bug survived until TM-06 asked for a 3x3 fill.
The old assertion was notEmpty on the whole response, which passes for an empty cell too — query_tile_cell answers is_empty: true rather than failing.

The test that caught it: a 3x3 region reported cells_filled 1, because to_coords parsed as (0, 0) and the rectangle collapsed onto its own corner. The echoed to_coords are asserted too — they name the parser directly instead of leaving a count to be explained.
The fill counted by a different tool than the one that reported it.
And on disk: the cells and the TileSet the setup built have to survive being packed, which is the only place a write that lived solely in the editor's memory shows up as missing.
